bhākuṭi:
bhakuṭī̆
bhākuṭi1 bhākuṭī bhū̆kuṭī̆, f. [cf S. bhrūkuṭī, bhṛkuṭī̆, bhrakuṭī̆], a frown; a grimace; M I 125,.20 (kupitā anattamanā ~iṃ akāsi, Se so; Be, Ce bhākuṭiṃ; Ee bhūkuṭiṃ); Sn 485 (~iṃ vinayitvāna, Be, Ee, Se so; Ce bhukuṭiṃ); Ja III 99,13* (cāleti kaṇṇaṃ ~iṃ karoti); V 296,1* (yadā maṃ ~iṃ katvā rājaputtī udikkhati, Be so; Ce bhukuṭiṃ katvā rājaputti udikkhasi; Ee, Se bhūkuṭiṃ katvā rājaputti udikkhasi; 296,8´ : kodhena valivisamaṃ nalāṭaṃ karitvā); VI 570,22´ foll. (n’ ev’ assa Maddībhakuṭī ti … Maddīdeviyā … kodhavasena mukhe ~ī nāhosi, Ce, Ee so; Se ~ī pi nāhosi; Be Maddī bhākuṭī ti … Maddī … bhākuṭi pi nāhosi); Vism 105,.14 (dosacarito … ~iṃ katvā sayati, Se so; Be bhākuṭiṃ; Ce, Ee bhākuṭikaṃ); Spk I 182,.4 (nalāṭikan ti ~iṃ); — see also bhākuṭika, bhākuṭikā, bhākuṭiya.

2bhākuṭi
mfn. [from bhakuṭī̆], frowning;? Ja VI 570,13* (n’ ev’ assa Maddī ~i na sandhīyati na rodati, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se Maddībhakuṭī; 570,22´ foll. Maddī ~ī ti … Maddī … kodhavasena ~i pi nāhosi, Be so; Ce, Ee Maddīdeviyā … kodhavasena mukhe bhakuṭī nāhosi; Se mukhe bhakuṭī pi nāhosi).
bujjhati:
1bujjhati
bodhati pr. 3 sg. [S. bodhati, budhyate], Dhātup 414 (budha avagamane); Sadd 481,.25 (budha avagamane: … ~ati buddho); — 1. realises; becomes or is aware of; recognises; D II 349,5* (littaṃ paramena tejasā gilam akkhaṃ puriso na ~ati); S I 74,11* (atisāraṃ na ~anti); A III 107,.5 (te abhāvitakāyā … kaṇhaṃ dhammaṃ okkamamānā na ~issanti); Dhp 136 (atha pāpāni kammāni karaṃ bālo na ~ati) = Th 146; Ja III 278,12* (bālo rahokammaṃ āvikubbaṃ na ~ati; 278,15´ : evaṃ kātuṃ na yuttan ti na jānāti); 331,7* (kasmā jālaṃ ca pāsaṃ ca āsajjāpi na ~asi); V 159,29* (kamalāsarisitthiyo tāyo ~esi māṇava; 160,7´ : tāyo jāneyyāsi); 495,1* (yo n’ attano maraṇaṃ ~asi tvaṃ); — 2. understands; S I 198,33* (dhammasmiṃ bhaññamānasmiṃ atthaṃ bālo na ~ati); Thī 453 (desente ajānantā na ~are ariyasaccāni); Ja II 264,22* (nāyaṃ dhammaṃ adhammaṃ vā atthānatthaṃ ca ~ati); VI 155,16* (~assu kho rājakali; 155,24´ : jāna sallakkhehi); Bv 1:67 (~assu amataṃ padaṃ); Mil 165,.27 (dhamme desiyamāne ye tattha sammā paṭipannā te ~anti ye pana micchā paṭipannā te patanti); Ps I 131,.1 foll. (bhavantaṃ Gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi bhajāmi … pajānāmi ~āmī ti, yesaṃ hi dhātūnaṃ gati attho buddhi pi tesaṃ attho tasmā gacchāmī ti imassa jānāmi ~āmī ti ayaṃ attho vutto); It-a I 87,.16 (jāneyyun ti ~eyyuṃ); Thī-a 52,.8 (tava attānam eva tāva ~assu yāthāvato jānāhi); Cp-a 18,.20 (cattāri ariyasaccāni ~ati etenā ti ariyamaggo bodhi); Sadd 395,.14 foll. (budha bodhane: bodhati buddho … bodhi, divādigaṇe pi ayaṃ dissati tatra hi ~atī ti rūpaṃ); — 3. realises, understands, the true nature of the world of experience; understands saṃsāra and the way to release from it; Bv 2:182 (yathā ye keci sambuddhā bodhimaṇḍamhi ~are tath’ eva tvaṃ mahāvīra ~assu jinabodhiyaṃ; cf Bv-a 119,.6 : ~are ti ~iṃsu); 26:12 (~issanti; Bv-a 293,.23 : ~issantī ti anāgate catusaccadhammaṃ paṭivijjhissantī ti); Mil 83,.24 (ekena kho mahārāja bojjhaṅgena ~ati: dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgenā ti); 169,.8 (tathāgato yena yena yogena bodhaneyyā ~anti tena tena yogena bodhaneyye bodheti); 348,4* (~eyya ca gihī dhamme dhutaṅgaṃ nipphalaṃ siyā); Ps I 83,.8 foll. (yāya … dhammasāmaggiyā ariyasāvako ~atī ti katvā bodhī ti vuccati, ~atī ti kilesasantānaniddāya uṭṭhahati cattāri vā ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhati nibbānam eva vā sacchikarotī ti) ≠ Ud-a 145,.18 foll.; Pj II 361,.9 (abhabbaparisā buddhasate pi dhammaṃ desente na ~ati bhabbaparisā sakkā bodhetun ti); Ap-a 142,.28 (buddhā sayaṃ ca ~anti pare ca bodhenti); Cp-a 18,.18 (~ati etthā ti rukkho bodhi); — 4. wakes; opens, blooms; Ps I 83,.13 (~atī ti kilesasantānaniddāya uṭṭhahati); Spk II 21,.8 (paripākagataṃ padumaṃ suriyarasmisamphassena avassaṃ ~issatī ti); Sadd 483,.26 foll. (budha ñāṇe budha vikasane budha niddakkhaye ti vuttaṃ hoti, ~ati bhagavā dhamme ~ati pabujjhati padumaṃ ~ati pabujjhati puriso); — part.pr. (a) bujjhanta, mfn., Bv 2:35 (uppajjante ca jāyante ~ante; Bv-a 83,.34 : anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhante); Dhp-a I 337,.6; (b) bujjhamāna, mfn., Sn 395; Bv 7:22; Dhp-a I 93,.25; — neg. abujjhamāna, mfn., Pj II 542,.6 = Nidd-a I 287,.30; — aor. 3 sg. (a) bujjhi, abujjhi, S I 48,31* (yo jhānam abujjhi buddho paṭilīnanisabho muni, Be so; Ce, Ee abudhā; Ee abuddhi) = A IV 449,10* (Be, Se so; Ce abudhā; Se anubujjhi); Nidd I 456,.11 foll. (bhagavā tena bodhiñāṇena sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ti ~i … yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamman ti ~i); Bv 2:210 (abujjhi); Mil 169,.25 (~i); Vism 209,.19 (cattāri saccāni attanā pi ~i aññe pi satte bodhesi); Pj II 394,.3 (vīṇā kacchato patitā … taṃ so patamānaṃ pi na ~i); Sadd 482,.1 (sabbaṃ pi ñeyyaṃ abujjhī ti buddho); (b) abujjhatha, Bv 7:22 (~amāno ca so buddho nāgamūle abujjhatha); — 3 pl. bujjhiṃsu, Th-a III 196,.30 (buddhā hi paṭhamaṃ cattāri saccāni ~iṃsu); Bv-a 119,.6; — inf. (a) boddhuṃ [ts], Th 167 (yaṃ kiccaṃ boddhum icchatā, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se bodhuṃ); Ja V 341,2* (boddhum arahanti āpadaṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee bodhum); (b) bujjhituṃ, Ja VI 310,.5 (yakkho saṅkhittena kathite cattāro sādhunaradhamme ~ituṃ asakkonto vitthārena pucchi); Ps I 100,.22 (aññātun ti jānituṃ ~ituṃ); Sadd 482,.24; (c) buddhuṃ, Sadd 482,.24; — absol. (a) bujjhitvā, Ap 28,.24 (sāmaṃ saccāni ~itvā); Mil 205,.6 (tathāgato ~itvā sabbadhamme parinibbuto upadhisaṅkhaye ti); Nidd-a I 176,.15 (ko hi nāma attasuññataṃ ~itvā puna sammohaṃ āpajjeyyā ti); Dīp 1:14; Sadd 482,.24; — neg. abujjhitvā, Cp-a 247,.9; (b) bujjhitvāna, Sadd 482,.24; — neg. abhujjitvāna, Cp 3:11:13 (Cp-a 247,.8 foll.: visaññībhāvena abujjhitvā ṭhito); — see also Sadd 482,.25 (bujjhitūna bu[d]dhiya bu[d]dhiyāna buddhā buddhāna); — part.perf.act. (a) buddhava(t), mfn., who has understood; who has woken; who has opened, expanded; It-a II 43,.17 foll. (kilesaniddāya accantavigamena buddhavā paṭibuddhavā ti buddho buddhiyā vā vikasitabhāvena buddhavā vibuddhavā ti buddho); Paṭis-a 537,.19 (catusaccaṃ buddhavā, ñātavā ti attho); (b) bujjhitava(t), mfn., who has realised, understood; Nidd-a I 177,.32 (ekakā va anācariyakā catusaccaṃ bujjhitavanto ti paccekabuddhā); Paṭis-a 207,.4 (taṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ paṭicca eko va anācariyako catusaccaṃ bujjhitavā ti paccekabuddho, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se bujjhitvā ti); — pass. pr. 3 sg. bujjhati2,? Pj I 219,.31 (so attho sukhaṃ ~atī ti); — pp (a) bujjhita, mfn., realised; understood; Peṭ 186,.18 (idaṃ viriyaṃ tassa tassa ~itassa aṅgan ti); Th-a III 5,.15 (sammāsambuddhehi ~itāni saccāni); — bujjhito ’mhi in Ee at Spk I 313,.14 is wr; Ce, Se pamādaṃ āpanno ’mhi vañcito ’mhi; Be vatamhi); — pp (b) buddha, mfn., see sv; — fpp (a) boddhabba (and, in Ee, bodhabba), (mf)n. [S. boddhavya], D II 246,.14 (gamanīyo samparāyo mantāya boddhabbaṃ kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, Be, Ce so; Ee bodhabbaṃ; Se voṭṭhabbaṃ; Sv 669,.11 foll.: mantā vuccati paññā tāya mantetabbaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ upaparikkhitabbaṃ ca jānitabbaṃ cā ti attho, karaṇatthe vā bhummaṃ … mantāya bujjhitabbaṃ ñāṇena jānitabban ti attho) ≠ A IV 136,.27 (Be, Ce so; Ee bodhabbaṃ; Se phoṭṭhabbaṃ; Mp IV 66,.2 : paññāya jānitabban ti); (b) bojjha, mfn. [S. bodhya], Nett 20,.31 (yaṃ bojjhaṃ taṃ catubbidhaṃ); (c) bujjhitabba, mfn., Nidd I 457,.1 (yaṃ kiñci ~itabbaṃ … sabbaṃ taṃ … ~i); Sv 669,.14 (mantāya ~itabbaṃ ñāṇena jānitabban ti); Ps III 405,.1 (~itabbaṃ ~itvā buddho jāto ’smī ti) = Pj II 455,.2 (Be so; Ce boddhabbaṃ; Ee bodhabbaṃ; Se bodhitabbaṃ) ≠ Th-a III 49,.19; Ap-a 430,.21 (vedena veditabbā ~itabbā ti vedā); —    caus. pr. 3 sg. (a) bodheti,        ~ayati, 1. (i) makes aware; makes (someone) understand (something); instructs; persuades; indicates, signifies; Ja VI 231,19´ (mama pitaraṃ ~essāmi); Ud-a 10,.14 (paṭī ti vā ayaṃ saddo pacchā ti etassa atthaṃ ~eti); It-a I 16,.25 (adhikavacanaṃ hi aññaṃ atthaṃ ~etī ti na punaruttidoso); Sadd 395,.18 (budha bodhane: bodhati … kārite pana ~eti icc ādīni); 716,.19 (~ayati); — (ii) esp. brings to understanding of the world of experience, of saṃsāra, and of the way to release from it; Ap 356,.28 (catusaccaṃ pakāsento ~eti janataṃ tadā); Bv 2:194 (bodhaneyyajanaṃ disvā … khaṇena upagantvāna ~eti taṃ mahāmuni); Mil 166,.25 (ete bodhaneyye satte ~eti); Sv 175,.17 (pavedetī ti ~eti ñāpeti pakāseti); Ud-a 133,.19 (ahaṃ sadevakaṃ lokaṃ … buddho ~essāmī ti); Pj II 51,.21 foll. (a) bodhenta, mfn., Mil 166,.9 (tathāgato paripakkamānase satte ~ento … dhammaṃ deseti, Be, Ee so; Ce, Se ~etuṃ); Ap-a 530,.20 (veneyyajanasaṅkhātapadumāni visesena ~ento arahattamaggādhigamena phullitāni karotī ti, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se pabodhento); (b) bodhaya(t), mfn., Ap 463,.26; (c) bodhayanta, mfn., Ap 306,.20; 474,.1; — aor. 3 sg. (a) bodhesi, Ja I 486,.19 (Be, Ce, Ee so; Se pabodhesi); VI 393,.30 (upāyen’ eva ~esi); Bv 5:7 (mahājanaṃ ~esi); Bv-a 287,.3 (suvaṇṇapātiṃ … paṭisotaṃ khipitvā Kālanāgarājaṃ supantaṃ ~esi); Vism 209,.19 (cattāri saccāni attanā pi bujjhi aññe pi satte ~esi); Mhv 5:264; (b) bodhayī̆, abodhayi, Bv 2:195 (abodhayi); 25:6 (~ayī); — inf. bodhetuṃ, Ja IV 393,.10 (Be, Ce, Ee so; Se pabodhetuṃ); VI 241,.28 (sā pitaraṃ ~etuṃ asakkontī); 389,7´ (asambodhan ti pi pāṭho, paresaṃ ~etuṃ ayuttan ti attho, so read with Be, Ce, Se); 397,16´ (vacībhedena jānāpetuṃ na sakkā tādisāni pan’ ettha kiccāni bherisaddasaṅkhasaddasaññāṇen’ eva ~entī ti, Ce, Ee so; Be bherisaṅkhasaddeh’ eva ~entī ti; Se pabodhentī ti); Mil 169,.4 (bodhaneyye satte ~etuṃ); Pj II 463,.7 (saññāpetun ti ñāpetuṃ ~etuṃ, niruttaraṃ kātun ti); — absol. (a) bodhetvā, Ja I 474,.20 (bodhisatto tāpase ~etvā); VI 405,.24 (te rājāno nānākāraṇehi ~etvā attano kathaṃ gaṇhāpetvā, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be sambodhetvā); Mp I 398,.14 (sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ti ~etvā desesi); (b) bodhetvāna, Ap-a 274,.22; (c) bodhayitvā, Ap 100,.19; — pp bodhita, mfn. [ts], made known; It-a I 42,.24 (tisso pi pariññā ~itā honti); Vv-a 152,.14; — neg. abodhita, mfn., Sv 910,.3 (abodhitatthā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee abodhitattā, prob. wr); Pj I 15,.18 (aññena abodhito); — fpp bodhaneyya, bodhanīya, mfn., Ap 352,.1 (bodhaneyyaṃ pajaṃ disvā); Bv 5:31 (bodhaneyye ca bodhayī, Se so; Be, Ce, Ee bodhanīye); Mil 169,.4 (dukkaraṃ cāpi mahārāja tathāgato karoti bodhaneyye satte bodhetuṃ, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se bodhanīye); Ap-a 272,.12 (bodhaneyyānaṃ dhammaṃ desente); Sadd 640,.21; — neg. abodhanīya, mfn., Nidd-a I 441,.28 (aññena abodhanīyato) = Paṭis-a 485,.13; — dubbodhaneyya, mfn., Pj II 87,.8 = Ap-a 168,.15; —      caus. pr. 3 sg. ussukka:
1ussukka
n. [S. autsukya], zealous activity, exertion, effort; concern; eagerness; Vin I 312,.15 (nahāne ~aṃ akāsi); II 289,.26 (tvaṃ mātugāmassa … pabbajjaṃ ~aṃ akāsi); IV 280,.6 (n ’eva sibbeti na sibbāpanāya ~aṃ karoti); D II 263,.7 (~aṃ udapādi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya); M I 324,.27 (tattha ~aṃ āpanno hoti); A V 195,.9 (na tathāgatassa evaṃ ~aṃ hoti, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se °-taṃ); Ud 4,.17 (pañcamattāni devatāsatāni ~aṃ āpannāni honti āyasmato Mahākassapassa piṇḍapātapaṭilābhāya); Ja II 429,.10 (ito paṭṭhāya amhākaṃ kattabbakiccesu ~aṃ āpajjā ti); Mil 116,.30 (brahmacariyesanāy’ eva ~aṃ āpanno); Vism 90,.8 (yo pan’ ettha navakammādisu ~aṃ vā āpajjati); — ifc see appô-; —     anussukka,   mfn. and n., 1. (mfn.) free from exertion or concern; Ps III 166,.27 (appossukkā ti ~ā); Ud-a 202,.2 (aññe … posetuṃ ~-tāya anaññaposino); — 2. (n.) lack of exertion, unconcern;? Cp-a 45,.15 (vipassanāya pi ~aṃ sabbattha anissaṅgatā ti evamādayo gunānubbhāvā, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se anussukkanaṃ); —      nirussukka,   mfn., free from exertion or concern; not making an effort; quiet, calm; Ja IV 336,.26 (baddhabhāvaṃ me ñatvā ~o acchissati, Ce so; Ee na ~o; Se anussukko; Be nirāsaṅko āgacchissati); V 354,.24; Spk I 296,.25 (appossukko ti … ~o); Ud-a 327,.13; — ussukka is often (wrongly) written for ussuka qv.

2ussukka
n. [= ussukka1, or from ussukkati qv sv ussakkati], (gr.t.t.) striving for, looking towards; moving forward (to another word, ie the characteristic of an absolutive); Sp 436,.25 (san ti upasaggo tena saddhiṃ °-vacanaṃ etaṃ sañciccā ti; Sp-ṭ [Be] II 250,.12 : °-vacanan ti pubbakālakiriyāvacanaṃ, ayaṃ hi samānakattukesu pubbāparakālakiriyāvacanesu pubbakālakiriyāvacanassa niruttivohāro); Paṭis-a 240,.31 (avijjā paṭiccā ti … avijjā paṭimukhaṃ etabbā gantabbā paṭiccā ti … avijjā paṭiccā ti °-vasena vā pāṭho … avijjā attano paccaye paṭicca pavattā ti); Tikap-a 232,.5 (iccā ti gamanussukkavacanaṃ etaṃ); — see also ussukkana.

ussuka
(often [wrongly] written ussukka), mfn. [S. utsuka], busy, zealously active; striving, eager (for); repining (for); Abh 727; D III 148,27* (guttīsu rakkhāvaraṇesu ~o); M III 131,.26 (kāmapariyesanāya ~o, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se ussukko); A III 38,13* (niccaṃ ātāpi ~o); Dhp 199 (susukhaṃ vata jīvāma ~esu anussukā); Sn 298 (kiccākiccesu ~ā); Th 494 (so ~o rasānugiddho atthaṃ riñcati); Ja II 383,10* (kim attham ~ā; 383,21´ : ~ā ti ukkaṇṭhitarūpā hutvā); VI 475,8* (ussukko te divārattiṃ sabbakiccesu vyāvaṭo, eds so); Ap 574,.14 (na cāhaṃ tatra ~ā); Vism 160,.1 (tadadhigamāya ussukkānaṃ ussāhajanakaṃ, eds so); Ud-a 116,.4 (vyāvaṭo ti ussukko, eds so); —     anussuka,   mfn., not busy; quiet, unconcerned; S I 15,23* (ke lokasmiṃ ~ā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr anussukkā); A IV 98,7* (vītalobhā ~ā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee anissukā, prob. wr); Ja II 232,18* (yattha bhutvā ca pītvā ca sayeyyātha ~o); VI 46,2* (ye ussukamhi lokamhi viharanti ~ā, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se ussukkamhi … ~ā); Pj II 449,.24 (janapado … ~o sakammanirato acalo …).
abbhāgata:
abbhāgata
mfn. and m. [pp of *abhi + āgacchati; S. abhyāgata], come; arrived (as a guest); an (uninvited) guest; A III 37,.25 (~e ca āsanodakena paṭipūjessāmā ti); Vv 1:5 (~ān’ āsanakaṃ adāsiṃ; Vv-a 24,.6 foll. : ~ānan ti abhi-āgatānaṃ sampatta-āgantukānan ti attho, duvidhā hi āgantukā atithi ~o ti, tesu kataparicayo āgantuko atithi akataparicayo ~o …); Ja IV 435,18´ (āsanūdakadāyīnan ti ~ānaṃ āsanaṃ ca udakaṃ ca dānasīlānaṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee adhigatānaṃ, prob. wr); Mil 157,.3; — abbhāgato in Ee at Ja VI 26,13* is wr for abbhāhato qv.

abhisambandhitabba:

mfn. [fpp of *abhi + sambandhati; cf S. abhisambadhnāti], to be connected (with); Pj II 385,.19 (etaṃ pabbajito ’mhī ti iminā ~aṃ, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se sambandhitabbaṃ); — see also abhisambandhitvā.
abhisambhoti:
abhisambhavati

1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
